generator: tools/motion_vectors/generate.py (copy of the local_retract cases of docs/motion/vectors.json for the backend CI image)

cases.description: Bolt in a fixed plate hole (concentric + end face): the free motion is the spin about the hole axis; a spin wish is ON the manifold, the retraction must return it exactly (fallback = the wish, as the projector reproduces it)
Pull the bolt 15 mm off the plate while spinning 20 deg: nearest mate-satisfying pose = back on the face, spun 20 deg
Slide the bolt 6/-3 mm sideways out of the hole: nearest = back on the axis (the grabbed pose stays ~1e-4 relative short of the wish)
Off-axis pin (axis 15 mm from the part origin, the CURVED mate of the investigation): a 4 deg turn of the part about its own origin is off the manifold; the retraction lands on the pin's orbit
Same pin, a 90 deg wish in one frame (an unrealistic hitch): the retraction converges but far (12 weighted mm) from the fallback pose; the distance guard rejects it and the fallback is shown
Angle mate 60 deg: tilting the part 3 deg further is off the cone; nearest = back on the cone
Angle mate: a spin about the cone axis (world z) keeps the angle: on the manifold, reproduced exactly
Distance mate 7 to a plane: wish 9 mm out -> nearest 7 mm (linear signed residual, side +1)
Nothing fixed (bolt AND plate move): a 3 deg turn of the grabbed bolt about x, the plate's wish is its current pose; both land on the manifold
Floating group: slide 4 mm along x and spin 10 deg: the plate rides along (minimal motion)
Floating group, 60 deg in one frame: with the hitch iterations it converges, but lands more than 0.5 max(L, d_wish) from the fallback: rejected
Floating group, 90 deg about y in one frame (a hitch the 8 iterations do not finish: residual > 1e-6): rejected, fallback shown
Concentric without rotation + end face: rank 6, no free motion; any wish returns the start
The local answer converges but lies more than 0.5 L from the fallback (a far projector output): rejected, fallback shown

Gear mate r = 0.5, k = -1 (two external gears on parallel shafts, each concentric to a fixed hole): gear A (grabbed) turned 30 deg - gear B must turn 15 deg the OPPOSITE way (the row dtheta_B - k r dtheta_A)
The same pair with Reverse (k = +1): gear A turned 30 deg turns gear B 15 deg the SAME way
Gear B grabbed (member 0): 60 deg on B turns A 120 deg the opposite way (the ratio read from B's side)
The frame starts where an earlier frame left the pair (A 80 deg, B -40 deg: on the relation measured from the ANCHOR poses at 0 deg); a further 10 deg on A -> B at -45
A turned 150 deg from its anchor (the twist is read in (-pi, pi]): B must be at -75 deg
Rack and pinion (62.832 mm per turn, k = +1): the pinion (grabbed) turned 90 deg pushes the rack 15.708 mm along +x (ds_B = k p / 2 pi dtheta_A)
The same with k = -1: the rack goes the other way (-15.708 mm for +90 deg)
The rack is grabbed (member 0) and pulled 20 mm along its rail: the pinion must turn 20 / 62.832 turn = 114.6 deg (the sense of k)
Screw, lead 2 mm, right-handed (k = +1), screw fixed: the nut turned 90 deg climbs 0.5 mm ((ds_B - ds_A) = k L / 2 pi (dtheta_B - dtheta_A))
Left-hand (k = -1): the same 90 deg turn lowers the nut 0.5 mm

The nut is pushed 0.9 mm up the screw (the hand pulls along the axis only): the nearest pose splits the correction between the climb and the turn the lead demands (a 0.9 mm climb is 162 deg of turn, shared in the weighted metric)
Concentric, aligned branch: tilting the pin 100 deg (past horizontal) must not turn it over - it stays pointing up (the old sign-agnostic cross() landed on the opposite root here)
Concentric, anti-aligned branch (pin upside down): the same 100 deg tilt keeps it pointing down
Concentric, anti-aligned: slide 6 mm along the axis and spin 30 deg - both free, reproduced exactly
Concentric, rotation locked on the half-turn spin branch (perp -1): a spin wish is blocked, the answer keeps the half-turn
Distance 7 on the -normal side: the part sits at z = -7; a wish at z = +2 (the other side of the plate) lands at -7, not +7
Distance 7 on the +normal side: a wish at z = -3 (through the plate) lands at +7
Distance 7, anti-aligned normals (the part's face points down at the plate): a 3 deg tilt wish is pulled back, the facing stays
Parallel, aligned: a 120 deg tilt wish (nearer the anti-aligned root) is pulled to the aligned one - z stays up
Parallel, anti-aligned: a spin about the shared direction is free and reproduced exactly
Angle 60 about a hinge, swing sense +: a wish that swings the lid 70 deg toward the flat position (past what the cone alone would hold) is pulled back to the +120 deg root, never across to -120
Angle 60 about a hinge, swing sense -: the mirror wish keeps the lid on the -120 deg root
Angle about a hinge: a slide along the hinge is free and reproduced exactly
Angle about a hinge, swing sense +, the lid wished onto the -120 root: the nearest point on the + branch, not the wished root
Coincident plane-plane on the ALIGNED branch (normals the same way, overlapping co-facing faces): a lift of 5 mm is pulled back onto the plane, slide and spin about z are free
Axis-axis distance 12 (squared residual scaled to mm): a pin 12 mm off the axis pulled 5 mm further out lands back at 12
Axis-axis distance 12, anti-aligned axes: a 100 deg tilt keeps the pin pointing down
Point-point distance 9 (a sphere around the fixed point, no root): a wish 2 mm further out and 1 mm sideways lands on the sphere again

5 boxes in a row on a plate, faces mated (group dof 3: slide x, y, spin z as one rigid row): the first box is slid 3 mm and turned 2 deg - the whole row must follow, 4 residual rows per mate (36 rows)
5-box row: the first box is lifted 2 mm off the plate and slid 3 mm - the lift is blocked, the slide drags the row

8 boxes in a row on a plate, faces mated (group dof 3: slide x, y, spin z as one rigid row): the first box is slid 3 mm and turned 2 deg - the whole row must follow, 4 residual rows per mate (60 rows)
8-box row: the first box is lifted 2 mm off the plate and slid 3 mm - the lift is blocked, the slide drags the row
Width (tab centred between two FREE bars; 3 members): the grabbed bar L is slid 4 mm along the gap normal - the gap mid-plane moves 2 mm, the tab follows (v4 `pair` side, 1 + 3 + 3 rows)
Width over free bars: the tab (grabbed first) is wished 6 mm off-centre - the nearest pose moves the tab back and shares the rest with the bars
Width over free bars: sliding the tab in y / z (in the planes) is free and the bars sit still - reproduced exactly
The same Width scene turned 35 deg about (1,2,3): bar L is pulled 3 mm along its own old x axis - the pair still averages the two origins
Width over free bars: bar L tilted 0.5 deg about z (nearly parallel faces, tiny cross product): the parallel rows pull it back
Width over free bars: bar L tilted 20 deg about y - the parallel rows pull the pair back to parallel; converges near the wish's nearest point
Width over free bars, anti-aligned branch (the tab starts turned a half turn): a 4 mm bar slide keeps the tab turned away
Anti-aligned Width: the tab tilted 100 deg about y (past horizontal) must not flip onto the aligned root
Width where bar R is fixed (the pair's second face is a frozen non-member) and bar L + tab move: bar L slid 4 mm drags the tab 2 mm
Width with a 3 mm offset from centre (distance, side +1): the tab sits at x = +3; bar R slid 6 mm out keeps it 3 mm past the NEW centre
Width offset 3 mm on the -normal side (side -1): the tab at x = -3; a wish that pushes the tab through the centre to x = +2 lands back on the -3 side

Width over FOUR free members (gap = two bars, tab = two halves; first tab face normal -x against the gap's +x = anti-aligned): bar L slid 4 mm - both mid-planes are averages of two origins (1 + 3 + 3 + 3 rows)
4-part Width: the left tab half is wished 8 mm away from the centre - the pair mid-plane follows only half of it, the rest of the group shares the correction
4-part Width: the right tab half tilted 10 deg about z - the tab pair's parallel rows pull it back to parallel
4-part Width, aligned (the first tab face is the right half's, normal +x): both bars slid apart 3 mm each - the gap centre stays, nothing else moves
4-part Width with the whole scene turned 50 deg about (3,-1,2): bar R pulled off 5 mm and bar L tilted 2 deg
Width plus a second mate on the tab (its bottom face on a fixed rail plane z = -4): lifting the tab off the rail and pulling it off-centre lands on both
